text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-The EU commission has once again postponed a decision on whether or not to impose a European Union anti-dumping duty on imports of Norwegian salmon.

-One out of six employees has no formal wage contract with the employer, a figure that is 66 percent higher than four years ago. The law says a contract should be signed if an employment lasts more than a month.

-Norway is an interesting insurance market because of its strong economy, Francis Loheac, a member of the International Insurance Association (CEA), says. He says he would not be surprised if foreign companies entered the Norwegian market.
-Christiania, the planned fruit of a merger between Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse and insurer Storebrand, could grow through friendly takeovers of other financial institutions.
-Norway's largest insurer Storebrand says it may take one of it's main shareholders, Aker RGI, to court if the company agrees to a process of redeeming preference shares in Storebrand.
-Einar Hope, director of the state competition council, wants to alter the law for issuing licenses to power plants.
-The herring oil industry in Norway exceeded 1.2 billion crowns in turnover last year and production is in full swing.
